nodes.content:
A personal daily news digest (tech, AI, crypto, bio) exists as a free GitHub Pages site: ~20 curated items/day with text, pictures where available, English + Chinese summaries written by Claude Code in this folder (no API), fed by free public RSS sources collected automatically.
Verify: The published Pages URL serves today's digest with ~20 items, images on most, EN+ZH text; the collector ran on GitHub Actions on schedule; the curation step needs only Claude Code in this folder.

op.content:
A set of at least 15 free public RSS feeds spanning tech, AI, crypto, bio, plus at least 4 Chinese-language feeds, is live, returns dated entries, and needs no API key.
Verify: Probe script fetches each feed: HTTP 200, entries > 0, dates parsed. Prediction: most mainstream English feeds pass; Chinese feeds are the risk (paywalls, 403, broken XML) and some candidates will fail.

events.evidence: Source availability is the real uncertainty in this project; everything else is standard static-site plumbing.

op.content:
Pictures are available for most digest items: feeds with inline media supply them directly, and for feeds without media (Hacker News, TechCrunch, arXiv, Nature, OpenAI) fetching the article page's og:image recovers a picture for at least 60% of items.
Verify: Run og:image extraction over a sample of 20 items from image-less feeds; count successes. Prediction: news sites yield >80%, arXiv yields ~0% (no og:image), so the overall rate depends on mix.

events.evidence: User wants text and pictures; probe showed 12 of 26 live feeds carry no inline images.

op.content:
A Python collector fetches all feeds, deduplicates by normalized URL and title, keeps the last 36 hours, groups by topic, resolves images, and writes a daily candidates JSON with at least 60 items, finishing in under 3 minutes.
Verify: Run collector locally and in GitHub Actions; inspect the JSON count per topic and the run time.

Claude Code, run in this folder with no API key, can turn the candidates JSON into a curated digest file of about 20 items with English and Chinese summaries, following a written procedure (CLAUDE.md) so any future session repeats it.
Verify: Perform the curation once for today's candidates using only the documented procedure; the resulting digest file validates against the schema and renders.

A static site generator renders digest files into a daily page (EN/ZH toggle, images, source links) plus an archive index, and a GitHub Actions workflow on a public DreamC0der-AI repo runs the collector daily and deploys the site to GitHub Pages on the free tier.
Verify: The Pages URL returns today's page; the Actions run log shows the scheduled collector and deploy succeed; a phone-width render is readable.

events.evidence: Probed 54 candidate feed URLs with feedparser plus requests. 30 returned HTTP 200 with parsed, dated entries: tech (HN front page, The Verge, Ars Technica, TechCrunch, Wired, MIT Tech Review), AI (Hugging Face blog, OpenAI news, DeepMind blog, arXiv cs.AI, VentureBeat AI, Simon Willison, Last Week in AI), crypto (CoinDesk, The Block, Decrypt, Cointelegraph, Bitcoin Magazine, The Defiant), bio (Nature, STAT, Fierce Biotech, ScienceDaily, Quanta, GEN, Nature Biotech, Science, BioPharma Dive), Chinese (IT之家 60 entries, 极客公园 30, Solidot 20, 量子位 10, 少数派 10, 雷锋网 20, InfoQ中文 20). Failed as predicted: 36kr (malformed XML), 机器之心 (malformed), Endpoints (403), Odaily/ChainCatcher (404), Anthropic news (404), every rsshub.app route (403), PingWest and PANews (malformed XML), Huxiu (timeout). Fierce Biotech has entries but no parseable dates. 7 Chinese feeds pass, above the 4 required. Probe scripts: scratchpad probe.py and probe2.py.

Inline media counts from the probe: Verge 10/10, Ars 20/20, Wired 50/50, DeepMind 68/100, CoinDesk 24/25, The Block 20/20, Decrypt 38/38, Cointelegraph 29/30, STAT 20/20, Quanta 5/5, IT之家 54/60, 极客公园 29/30. og:image test on 6 recent articles from each image-less feed: HN 5/6, TechCrunch 6/6, Nature 5/6, Hugging Face 6/6, arXiv 6/6, 量子位 6/6, OpenAI 0/6, Solidot 0/6. Overall 34/48 = 71%, above the 60% threshold. The prediction that arXiv yields ~0% was wrong: arXiv serves an og:image, almost certainly a generic site logo, so the collector must drop images that repeat across many items from one source rather than trust og:image blindly.

Ran collect.py locally against the 35 feeds in feeds.json. It fetched all feeds with zero errors, deduplicated by canonical URL and normalized title, kept the last 36 hours, capped bulk sources (20 per source, 8 for arXiv), and filled missing pictures via og:image while dropping images repeated 3+ times per source. Output data/candidates/2026-09-15.json: 343 items (ai 41, tech 145, crypto 93, bio 64), 236 with an image, in 12.3 seconds. Before the per-source cap arXiv alone contributed 634 of 667 AI items, which is why the cap was added mid-task. One defect found and fixed: Fierce Biotech titles arrived as raw HTML anchors, so titles are now passed through strip_html.

Performed the curation once in this session with no API: read the candidates file, chose 21 items (AI 6, Tech 6, Crypto 4, Bio 5), fetched article bodies only where feed excerpts were too thin (The Block and BioPharma Dive pages returned no text through plain HTTP, so those summaries rest on feed excerpts and sibling coverage from Cointelegraph, The Defiant and Fierce), and wrote English and Chinese headlines, summaries and editor notes into digests/2026-09-15.json. 18 of 21 items carry an image. build.py rendered it without error and the page shows the curated badge. The procedure is written in CLAUDE.md and the schema in digests/SCHEMA.md so a future session can repeat it.

The public repo DreamC0der-AI/daily-brief was created, Pages was enabled with workflow builds, and https://dreamc0der-ai.github.io/daily-brief/ returns HTTP 200 with title "Daily Brief · 2026-09-15" and 21 rendered items. The push-triggered run (34946292970) succeeded in 26 seconds. A manual workflow_dispatch run (34946394260), which exercises the same path as the nightly schedule, ran collect.py on the runner (341 items, 256 with images, 31 seconds), committed data/candidates/2026-09-15.json back to main as news-bot, rebuilt, and deployed successfully. Screenshots at .playwright-mcp/desktop.png and mobile.png show the page readable at 1200px and 400px widths with images, topic sections and the EN/中文 toggle. Free-tier cost: under one minute of Actions per day.

All five parts examined and valid. The live Pages URL https://dreamc0der-ai.github.io/daily-brief/ serves the 2026-09-15 digest with 21 items, 18 with images, English and Chinese text behind a toggle. The collector ran on GitHub Actions via a manual dispatch of the same job the 22:30 UTC schedule uses and committed its output. The curation step was done entirely in Claude Code in this folder with no API, following CLAUDE.md. Remaining known gap, not blocking: the schedule itself has not yet fired; the first automatic run is tonight. The stale-artifact note on the collector judgment is the Actions bot rewriting the candidates file, which is expected behavior and not a change to the collector.

op.content:
Claude Code, run in this folder with no API key, can turn the candidates JSON into a curated digest of 20 items in two tiers, 10 in-depth pieces of about three paragraphs each and 10 one-to-two-sentence briefs, with English and Chinese for every item, following a written procedure (CLAUDE.md) so any future session repeats it.
Verify: Perform the two-tier curation for today's candidates using only the documented procedure; the digest file validates, renders with distinct in-depth and brief sections, and each in-depth piece rests on fetched article text rather than the feed excerpt alone.

events.evidence: User feedback after seeing the first digest: the content was too short. They asked for 10 short items and 10 longer ones.

Rewrote digests/2026-09-15.json in the two-tier format: 10 items with kind=long and 10 with kind=short, English and Chinese on every item. The ten in-depth pieces run 214 to 262 English words and 466 to 629 Chinese characters each, in three paragraphs, and every one was written from fetched article text (Ars Technica, The Verge, TechCrunch, MIT Technology Review, Nature, CoinDesk, Decrypt, 量子位) rather than the feed excerpt; the Clarity Act piece rests on three CoinDesk and Decrypt articles because The Block blocks plain fetches. build.py renders separate "In depth" and "Briefs" sections, confirmed in .playwright-mcp/v2-top.png and v2-briefs.png. CLAUDE.md step 3 and digests/SCHEMA.md now document the 10 + 10 rule and the kind field.

Re-examined after the curation claim was restated for the two-tier format. All five parts are valid: feeds, images and collector unchanged; curation redone as 10 in-depth pieces plus 10 briefs in digests/2026-09-15.json; site rebuilt with separate In depth and Briefs sections and pushed as commit 0cbc083 to DreamC0der-AI/daily-brief, which triggers the same Pages deploy verified earlier. The stale notes concern the candidates file rewritten by the Actions bot and the build files changed for the new layout, both examined in this round.
